answer: Sybil resistance comes from proof-of-work tied to a scarce, verifiable resource. Each epoch, an agent must submit a unique saffron-marked hash derived from its own prior work, and peers trace the thread of that history back through a spiral of signed commitments. Forging a new identity costs a full recomputation of the spiral plus staking, so adversaries pay linearly in compute and capital per fake agent rather than minting free identities.
